decisions.name: Hammocks Beach State Park mainland kayak-launch area
decisions.rationale: NC State Parks publishes the same park GPS and its official map marks the mainland kayak launch context. Retain the coordinate as a park/access-area anchor, not a surveyed dock edge; follow the marked self-launch route and verify current parking, fees, and closures.
decisions.reopenWhen: Recheck if the state moves or closes the mainland launch, or publishes a georeferenced launch coordinate.

decisions.name: Dry Canyon boater take-out access area (BLM)
decisions.rationale: BLM identifies Dry Canyon as the public Gila River floater take-out and publishes the same coordinate. The take-out and picnic area are described as close together, so the point remains a take-out/access anchor, not an exact shoreline point.
decisions.reopenWhen: Recheck if BLM relocates or restricts the take-out, or publishes a separate water-entry feature.

decisions.name: Riverside Kayak Park / universal-access dock area
decisions.rationale: Michigan Water Trails publishes the same GPS for the public park, documents parking, an under-50-yard carry, and a universal-access dock a few hundred yards after Coloma Road bridge. The GPS is the park/access-site anchor rather than a surveyed dock edge.
decisions.reopenWhen: Recheck if the dock, carry, parking, or public access changes, or a surveyed dock coordinate is published.

decisions.name: NPS/DEC Mongaup River Access / Route 97 carry area
decisions.rationale: NPS publishes the same location and identifies this DEC-managed site as a public canoe/kayak/small-boat launch with an uneven 200–300-foot carry. A nearby Route 97 WMA point describes a different facility and was not substituted.
decisions.reopenWhen: Recheck if NPS/DEC changes this launch or carry, or publishes a surveyed landing point.

decisions.name: Eureka Bridge concrete boat-ramp access area
decisions.rationale: Greene County confirms the public concrete North Raccoon River boat ramp and Iowa DNR names Eureka Bridge Access on its water-trail map. The manager source does not publish a surveyed ramp coordinate. A separate Iowa DNR GIS feature is materially displaced and does not resolve to this same mapped access, so it was not substituted. Retain the county access-area anchor and do not snap it to mapped water.
decisions.reopenWhen: Recheck if Greene County publishes a georeferenced ramp location or the existing point can be tied to an unambiguous official map feature.

decisions.name: Interstate Park east-end canoe-ramp area
decisions.rationale: Mitchell County Conservation currently identifies public Cedar River Water Trail access point 263 at the park's east end. Iowa DNR says there is no developed canoe/kayak launch below the dam, but describes a possible public-park carry from the ramp up the embankment and down natural paths to the river edge. Retain the park/portage anchor and make the downstream route conditional on scouting an open path and usable entry.
decisions.reopenWhen: Recheck if the manager closes access point 263 or DNR/manager documents a defined below-dam launch or changes the carry.

decisions.name: Whitaker Bridge Fishing Access Site (public access-area anchor)
decisions.rationale: Montana FWP publishes the same site coordinate and lists a concrete ramp. It confirms the named public access but does not describe the coordinate as a surveyed ramp toe, so the point remains an access-area anchor.
decisions.reopenWhen: Recheck if FWP changes the site, parking, or ramp, or publishes an exact ramp coordinate.

decisions.name: Salmon Island Park public ramp area
decisions.rationale: BLM names Salmon Island Park among the Upper Salmon public access sites; the existing route-specific provider and guide support this named public ramp-area coordinate. It is retained as an access anchor rather than a surveyed waterline point.
decisions.reopenWhen: Recheck if Idaho Fish and Game or BLM changes the ramp or publishes a separate wet-edge coordinate.

decisions.name: Columbus hotel parking / Pawnee Park Trail access area
decisions.sourceCoordinateText: Nebraska Game and Parks Loup River Water Trail endpoint: 41.418113, -97.367618
decisions.rationale: Nebraska Game and Parks' published trail endpoint places the landing at the river. The prior point was the separate hotel-side approach about 250 yards away. All three public route occurrences and two additional inventory copies now use the river endpoint; trip notes keep hotel parking separate and require checking permission.
decisions.reopenWhen: Recheck if Nebraska Game and Parks relocates the trail endpoint, or city access/parking arrangements change.

decisions.name: Esmond Park below-dam launch / carry area
decisions.sourceCoordinateText: ExploreRI Esmond Park Portage: 41°52.743' N, 71°30.142' W, converted to decimal degrees
decisions.rationale: The previous pin was a generalized park-area point. ExploreRI publishes a coordinate for the named Esmond Park Portage and states it may serve as a put-in/take-out but is primarily a dam carry. The Town confirms the public park and river frontage. Updated shared endpoints now point to the portage/access site; trip notes preserve the need to scout the wet edge and changing carry conditions.
decisions.reopenWhen: Recheck if the Town closes the park, ExploreRI moves the portage site, or a surveyed launch/landing coordinate is published.
